title: PTGui Viewpoint Correction: Masking for Offset Images, Floor-Only Alignment, and a Cologne Cathedral Counterexample

locations.name: Cologne Cathedral (top) – demonstration counterexample

summary: This PTGui Pro tutorial explains Viewpoint Correction, a feature used to integrate images captured from offset viewpoints (not at the no-parallax point) into a single panorama. The presenter emphasizes that the mapped area must be approximately flat, and demonstrates the workflow: enable Viewpoint Correction, mask everything not on the ground surface, then run Align Images and the Optimizer to verify results. A practical example shows masking the floor so only the flat surface is used, yielding a clean floor join; a counterexample (top of Cologne Cathedral) demonstrates the problems that arise when masking is not applied. The lesson underscores staying reasonably close to the no-parallax point to improve automatic control point generation and keep image deformation manageable.

sections.title: Introduction to Viewpoint Correction and its limitations
sections.description: The tutor introduces Viewpoint Correction, clarifies it is a PTGui Pro feature, and explains why offset viewpoints occur (e.g., to avoid ground-level occlusions) and why the no-parallax point is the ideal reference.

sections.title: Correct workflow: enable, mask, and align
concepts: Enable Viewpoint Correction in the Project Assistant
Mask everything not on the ground surface
Masking excludes areas from panorama and CP generation
sections.description: Demonstrates the practical steps: activate Viewpoint Correction, create a mask to isolate the ground/floor area, and run Align Images followed by the Optimizer to verify a clean floor join.

sections.title: What happens if masking and workflow are not followed
concepts: Effect of not masking when using Viewpoint Correction
Unmasked areas lead to undesired control points
Masking prevents walls and non-ground areas from influencing alignment
sections.description: Shows a counterfactual where alignment appears poor without masking, then explains that even with Viewpoint Correction enabled, missing masks cause control points to form on walls and other non-ground surfaces, degrading results.

sections.title: Counterexample and practical takeaways
concepts: Masking the non-floor areas is essential
Undoing masking can ruin the panorama; masking prior CP generation is easier
sections.description: Presents a scenario on the cathedral roof to illustrate the catastrophe of removing non-ground masks, then reiterates the floor-only approach yields a correct panorama when masking is applied.
